root_cause_label: Naive Motion Peak Heuristic Without Domain-Appropriate Foot Tracking
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent committed to a global motion intensity peak heuristic for detecting hurdle jump takeoff and landing, ignoring a clear forewarning that the detected peaks occurred at the very end of the video (frames 108/113 of 119) where the athlete was exiting rather than jumping, and never adopted the domain-appropriate approach of tracking foot-level position.
t_err_evidence: In step 6 the agent writes jump_analyzer.py implementing background subtraction followed by motion peak detection, using the first and last peaks of motion intensity as takeoff and landing. This heuristic cannot reliably distinguish a jump from running strides or exit from frame, and the agent chose this approach despite step 5 showing peaks at frames 108 and 113 out of 119 — the very end of the video where the athlete would be exiting rather than jumping.
t_commit_evidence: The script is written to disk in step 6 with the flawed algorithm fully baked in. All subsequent steps merely install a missing dependency (step 8), run the script (step 9), verify format (steps 10-13), and claim completion — no algorithmic change is ever made after this point.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacks domain knowledge about how to properly detect a hurdle jump in a video. The correct approach requires tracking foot-level horizontal displacement relative to a hurdle barrier; instead, the agent relied on global motion intensity peaks which conflate the athlete's continuous running motion with the actual jump event. This is a CV task-specific knowledge gap, not a misread of output or a tooling failure.
forewarning_evidence: Step 5 produces peaks at frames 108 and 113 out of 119 frames. The agent explicitly noted in step 6 that 'these seem very late in the video' and 'the peaks might be at the very end when the athlete exits the frame', which is exactly the right concern. Despite this self-doubt, the agent switched to a slightly different implementation but kept the same peak-finding logic.
